What we
believe.

The full statement of faith of Faith Life Community Ministries, a Bible-based, Christ-centered church in Winnipeg. Eleven beliefs in four big ideas, with every Scripture reference one tap away.

Read the statement Explore it in Growth Track

01

God

Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

One God in three persons, at the centre of everything we believe.

God

God is the Creator and Ruler of the universe. He has eternally existed in three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. These three are co-equal and are one God.

Scripture references
Genesis 1:1, 26, 27Psalm 90:21 Peter 1:22 Corinthians 13:14

Jesus Christ

Jesus Christ is the Son of God. He is co-equal with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Jesus was both fully God and fully human, was born of a virgin and lived a perfect, sinless human life. He offered Himself as the perfect sacrifice for the sins of all people by dying on a cross. He arose from the dead after three days to demonstrate His power over sin and death. He ascended to Heaven’s glory and will return someday to reign as King of Kings and Lord of Lords.

Scripture references
Matthew 1:22-23Isaiah 9:6John 1:1-5John 8:58John 14:10-30Hebrews 4:14-151 Corinthians 15:3-4Romans 1:3-4Acts 1:9-11Philippians 2:5-111 Timothy 6:14-15Titus 2:13

The Holy Spirit

The Holy Spirit is a divine person, co-equal with the Father and the Son. He is present in the world to make people aware of their need for Jesus Christ. He lives in every Christian from the moment of salvation. He provides the Christian with the power for living, enables understanding of Biblical truth and guides them in righteous living. He provides every Christian with spiritual gifts for service. As Christians, we seek to live under His control daily.

Scripture references
2 Corinthians 3:17John 16:7-13John 14:16-17Acts 1:81 Corinthians 2:122 Corinthians 3:16Ephesians 1:13Ephesians 5:18Galatians 5:25
02

The Bible

God’s Word to us.

The supreme source of truth for what we believe and how we live.

The Bible

The Bible is God’s Word to us. It was written by human authors under the supernatural guidance of the Holy Spirit. It is the supreme source of truth for Christian beliefs and living. Because it is inspired by God, it is truth without any mixture of error.

Scripture references
2 Timothy 1:132 Timothy 3:162 Peter 1:20-21Psalm 119:105, 160Psalm 12:6Proverbs 30:5
03

People and salvation

Lost, found and kept.

Who we are, how we are saved, and why we can be sure of it.

Humanity

People are the supreme object of God’s creation, originally created in the image and likeness of God. Humanity fell through disobedience, incurring both physical and spiritual death. All people are sinners by nature and sinners by choice and this separates them from the life of God. Only through the atoning work of Jesus Christ can anyone be saved and restore a relationship with God.

Scripture references
Genesis 1:27Psalm 8:3-6Psalm 51:1-8Isaiah 53:6Isaiah 59:1-2Romans 3:23Romans 5:12

Salvation

Salvation is by grace through faith. It is God’s free gift to us, but we must accept it. We can never make up for our sin by self-improvement or good works. Only by trusting in Jesus Christ as God’s offer of forgiveness can anyone be saved from sin’s penalty. When we turn in repentance from our self-ruled life and turn to Jesus in faith, we are saved. Eternal life begins the moment one receives Jesus Christ into his life by faith.

Scripture references
Romans 6:23Ephesians 2:8-9John 14:6John 1:12Titus 3:5Galatians 3:26Romans 5:1

Assurance of salvation

We believe that all the redeemed, once saved, are kept by God’s power and are thus secure in Christ forever. We believe that it is the privilege of believers to rejoice in the assurance of their salvation through the testimony of God’s Word which, however, clearly forbids the use of Christian liberty as an occasion to the flesh.

Scripture references
John 6:37-40John 10:27-30Romans 8:1, 38-391 Corinthians 1:4-81 Peter 1:4-5Romans 13:13-14Galatians 5:13Titus 2:11-15
04

Forever things

Church, ordinances and eternity.

Life together now, and the hope that lies ahead.

The Church

The Church consists of all those who have been saved through faith in Jesus Christ. Christ is the Head of the Church, whose members have been commissioned by Him to go into all the world as a witness, preaching the gospel to all nations. The local church is an autonomous, local body of believers in Christ who are joined together for the worship of God, for teaching of the Word of God, for prayer, fellowship and the proclamation of the Gospel, and for observance of the ordinances of Baptism and the Lord’s Supper. The local church is governed by the principles found in Scripture.

Scripture references
Matthew 16:18Acts 2:41-471 Corinthians 12:12-14Colossians 1:18Hebrews 10:25

Baptism & the Lord’s Supper

Jesus instructed His disciples to remember His death and resurrection. He gave the Church two visible symbols (called “ordinances”) as reminders. These two ordinances are Baptism and the Lord’s Supper. While we respect all acts of spiritual obedience, the Bible teaches that Baptism is to be done by immersion, following salvation, as a one-time act of obedience and identification with Jesus Christ as Lord. The Lord’s Supper is an ongoing symbol remembering our Lord’s death, burial, resurrection and promised return. Each individual must decide his or her own participation in these ordinances. Regardless, we do not regard anyone’s participation in these practices as a means of salvation.

Scripture references
Matthew 28:18-20Matthew 26:26-291 Corinthians 11:23-32Colossians 2:12

Eternity

People were created to exist forever in eternity. We will either exist eternally separated from God by sin, or eternally with God through forgiveness and salvation through Jesus Christ. To be eternally separated from God is Hell. To be eternally in union with Him is eternal life. Heaven and Hell are real places of eternal existence.

Scripture references
John 3:16John 17:3Romans 6:231 Thessalonians 4:16-17Revelation 20:15

Christ’s return

We believe in the “blessed hope,” the personal, imminent return of Christ Who will rapture His Church prior to the seven-year tribulation period. At the end of the Tribulation, Christ will personally and visibly return with His saints to establish His earthly Messianic Kingdom which was promised to the nation of Israel.

Scripture references
Psalm 89:3-4Daniel 2:31-45Zechariah 14:4-111 Thessalonians 1:101 Thessalonians 4:13-18Titus 2:13Revelation 3:10Revelation 19:11-16Revelation 20:1-6
